To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extinction of species is a global public bad and that international environmental agreements are the only effective means of internalising the global costs of this public bad.

the decline of biological diversities is the result of a dynamic externality that arises from a particular form of development process; that the fundamental force causing this decline is relative underinvestment, and that international environmental regulation of extinction is the means to correct for this underinvestment and to control the decline.

the decline of biological resources is the result of a dynamic externality inherent in the development process, that the regulation of extinction may be effected by the internalisation of these global benefits through international environmental agreements, and that the three distinct international environmental agreements that may be employed in this process are international franchise agreements, international wildlife trade regimes, and international intellectual property right regimes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the international regulation of extinction, the decline of biological resources, and the creation of mechanisms to control this decline.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
international agreements are the only means by which to internalise the global benefits of biological diversity.

we have attempted to explain the decline of biological resources as the result of an economic dynamic inherent within the process of development, and we have attempted to show that the decline of these resources may be regulated through international agreements.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the international regulation of extinction is not merely a matter of international cooperation, but of the international regulation of development.

the international regulation of extinction must take into consideration the particular form of dynamic externalities that are inherent in the global development process, and which give rise to the decline of biological species.

the international regulation of extinction is best conceived in terms of a set of international agreements to internalise global benefits from the existence of biological diversity, rather than in terms of a single international agreement to regulate the rate of decline of biological diversity.
